legal_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me complete step n1 of our IP assignments process: compile a complete list of all team members (founders and employees) who need signed IP assignment agreements (PIIAs).

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in your configured credentials or environment, specifically:
1. Confirmation that you have access to our {{vendor}} payroll account (using my configured credentials), or if not, ask me to confirm access is set up.
2. A list of founders (and any other equity holders or advisors doing work for the company) who may not appear in payroll, since founders are sometimes not run through payroll in the early days.

Once you have access, use the {{vendor}} dashboard or its API to retrieve the current roster of employees, including full legal name, employment start date, and employment status (active/terminated). Do this in words — do not assume or output specific endpoint calls.

Cross-reference this payroll list with the founder list I provide, so the final roster includes everyone: all active employees from {{vendor}} plus all founders/advisors not in payroll.

Produce a clean table with columns: Full Name, Role (Founder/Employee/Advisor), Start Date, Status (Active/Terminated), Source (Payroll or Manual). Flag any terminated employees separately, since they may still need a signed PIIA retroactively if one is missing.

When done, report back to me with: (1) the total headcount found, (2) the complete table, (3) any discrepancies or people you couldn't confirm status for, and (4) a short note on any access issues encountered with {{vendor}}. This list will be used in the next step to check PIIA signature status, so completeness and accuracy are critical.

legal_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me generate individual Proprietary Information and Inventions Assignment (PIIA) agreements for every founder and employee of my company. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the legal company name and state/country of incorporation, (2) a list of all founders and employees who need a PIIA, each with full legal name, role/title, and start date, (3) any prior inventions each person wants excluded (or confirmation there are none), and (4) whether the company uses a standard at-will employment structure.

Using this information, draft a separate PIIA document for each individual using standard, widely-used PIIA language covering: assignment of inventions and IP created during engagement, confidentiality/non-disclosure of proprietary information, disclosure of prior inventions, return of company property, and a signature block with date lines for the individual and a company representative. Personalize each draft with the correct name, role, start date, and any listed prior-invention exclusions. Save each draft as a clearly named file (e.g., PIIA_[FullName].docx or .pdf) in a dedicated folder.

Do not send these documents for signature, contact anyone, or submit anything — sending for signature and execution remains a human step. Your job is only to prepare accurate, ready-to-review drafts.

When done, report back: the full list of individuals for whom PIIAs were generated, the file names/locations of each draft, any missing information you had to flag (e.g., unclear start dates or unresolved prior inventions), and a short note confirming each draft is ready for legal review before circulation for signature.

legal_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me manage the legal review of our PIIA (Proprietary Information and Inventions Assignment) template as part of our IP assignments process. This step requires an outside attorney to substantively review the template for state-specific IP-assignment and consideration requirements — that legal judgment call remains a human step and cannot be performed by you.

Your job is to prepare everything needed and then track status until the review is complete. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) the current PIIA template file or link, (b) the name/contact of the attorney or law firm handling review, (c) which state(s) or jurisdictions apply to our founders/employees, and (d) any deadline I have in mind.
2. Draft a concise transmittal email to the attorney that: attaches or links the template, states the purpose (confirm the PIIA satisfies state-specific IP-assignment and consideration requirements before company-wide use), lists the relevant jurisdictions, and asks for explicit sign-off or requested edits by the deadline I provide.
3. Prepare a simple tracking log (date sent, attorney contact, jurisdictions covered, status, follow-up date) so I can monitor progress.
4. Do not send the email or represent that I am submitting anything for signature — just prepare the draft and log, then stop for human sign-off before it goes out.
5. Once I confirm the email was sent, note that the result lands asynchronously — set a reminder to check back (e.g., in 5-7 business days) and ask me periodically whether a response has arrived so we can update the tracking log.

Report back with: the drafted email, the tracking log template, and a clear note confirming this step is now in third-party-wait status pending attorney review, with a suggested follow-up date for polling status.

legal_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me send Proprietary Information and Invention Assignment Agreements (PIIAs) to all founders and employees using {{vendor}}, our configured e-signature/legal-ops platform. Approval is required before anything is actually sent, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: (1) the full list of founders and employees who need a PIIA, with their legal names and email addresses, (2) the PIIA template to use (or confirm one already exists in {{vendor}}), and (3) any routing/signing order requirements (e.g., company signatory who countersigns after the individual).

Then, using {{vendor}}'s configured credentials:
1. Locate or upload the correct PIIA template in the platform.
2. Populate the template with each recipient's name and details, either individually or via a bulk-send workflow if the platform supports it.
3. Set up the signature routing for each document so it goes to the individual first and then to the appropriate company signatory, if required.
4. Stage all documents as drafts ready to send — do not click send or finalize.
5. Prepare a summary checklist listing each recipient, their document status (drafted/staged), and the routing order.

Done looks like: every founder and employee has a correctly populated, properly routed PIIA staged in {{vendor}}, ready to send, with no documents actually dispatched yet.

Report back with: the list of staged documents, confirmation of the template and routing used, and any recipients you couldn't prepare (missing email, name, etc.). Then stop for human sign-off before sending any documents.

legal_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track and follow up on unsigned IP assignment agreements (PIIAs) for founders and employees, using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) the list of founders/employees who should have signed PIIAs, (2) my configured {{vendor}} credentials/access, and (3) any reminder cadence or expiration policy I want enforced (e.g., remind every 3 days, expire after 14 days).

Actions to take:
1. Using the {{vendor}} dashboard or API, check the status of all pending PIIA envelopes and identify which recipients have not yet signed.
2. For each unsigned envelope, verify the signing order is correct and confirm automatic reminders and an expiration date are set; configure them if missing.
3. Where {{vendor}} supports it, subscribe to webhook events so you're notified automatically when a document is signed, declined, or expires, and note this setup so I know monitoring is active.
4. Compile a status report listing each person, envelope status (pending/signed/expired), last reminder sent date, and days outstanding.
5. For any envelope stuck beyond the agreed threshold, draft a polite follow-up message (email or in-app) I can send, but do not send it yourself unless I've asked you to automate outreach explicitly.
6. Since final completion depends on the recipient actually signing — a step outside your control — this remains a human step for the signer's action; your job is to prepare, monitor, and poll/verify status until all are resolved.

Done looks like: every outstanding PIIA has reminders/expiration configured, a current status report is compiled, and you've confirmed whether webhook or polling-based monitoring is active for future updates.

Report back with: the full status table, which envelopes still need follow-up, confirmation of reminder/expiration settings applied, and confirmation of webhook subscription status (or a note that polling will be used instead).

legal_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me complete step legal_003:n6 of our IP assignments process: filing executed copies of signed PIIAs into our cloud storage system, {{vendor}}.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the folder location or path in {{vendor}} where signed IP assignment agreements should live, (2) the list of executed PIIA files (or where to find them, e.g., an e-signature platform's completed documents folder) that need to be uploaded, and (3) any custom metadata fields we want tracked (e.g., employee name, signature date, document type, effective date).

Using my configured credentials, please:
1. Confirm or create the designated folder in {{vendor}} for executed PIIAs.
2. Upload each executed PIIA file into that folder via the {{vendor}} API — use the resumable/large-file upload method for files above a few MB, and the simple upload method for smaller files.
3. Set custom metadata/properties on each uploaded file (employee name, signing date, document type) using {{vendor}}'s metadata API, so records can be queried later.
4. Verify version history is enabled for these files so future revisions can be listed and restored within the platform's retention window.
5. List the final contents of the folder to confirm all expected PIIAs are present and correctly tagged.

Done looks like: every signed PIIA is uploaded to the correct folder in {{vendor}}, tagged with accurate metadata, and confirmed present via a listing call.

Report back with: the folder location, a list of uploaded files with their metadata values, any files that failed to upload or lacked metadata, and any files you couldn't locate — flag those so I can supply or re-send them.
